root_cause.text: In dm-thin's `rebalance_children()`, collapsing a one-entry internal btree node into its child copied the child’s grandchild pointers into the parent without incrementing those grandchildren’s metadata reference counts when the child block was shared, leaving refcounts inconsistent with actual references.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly states that when the child “is shared (it has reference count > 1), we won't free it, so there would be two pointers to each of the grandchildren nodes” but “the reference counts of the grandchildren is not increased”; the patch fixes this by checking `dm_tm_block_is_shared()` and calling `inc_children(info->tm, dm_block_data(child), vt)` before `memcpy()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix rebalance of single-entry nodes by preserving child reference counts when copying from a shared child block.
intent_record.what: In the rebalance_children() path for a node with exactly one entry, the change adds an is_shared variable, calls dm_tm_block_is_shared(info->tm, b, &is_shared) before dm_tm_read_lock(), returns on error from that call, and conditionally invokes inc_children(info->tm, dm_block_data(child), vt) after locking the child block when the child block is shared, before copying the child node data into the parent with memcpy().
intent_record.how: At runtime, when collapsing a single-entry internal node by copying its child into it, the code now detects whether the child block is shared and, if so, increments the referenced children counts of that child before overwriting the parent with its contents. This preserves correct reference accounting for shared subtree metadata and avoids losing child references during the in-place replacement.

candidates.rationale: This raw copy collapses the one-entry internal node by copying the shared child block's contents, including grandchild pointers, into the parent without performing the needed metadata reference count increments for those newly referenced grandchildren.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement performs a raw copy of the child internal node into the parent during collapse. When the child block is shared, the copied grandchild pointers become newly referenced by the parent, but this copy does not increment their metadata reference counts, causing refcount state to diverge from the actual references.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant logic is fully visible in `rebalance_children()`. In the `if (le32_to_cpu(n->header.nr_entries) == 1)` case, the code collapses a one-entry internal node by read-locking its child and then doing a raw full-block copy: `memcpy(n, dm_block_data(child), dm_bm_block_size(dm_tm_get_bm(info->tm)));` followed by `dm_tm_dec(info->tm, dm_block_location(child));`. This copies the child's contents, including child/grandchild pointers, into the parent/root node, but there is no call here to increment metadata reference counts for those copied grandchildren when the child block was shared. The only incrementing logic shown elsewhere is in `init_child()`, where `dm_tm_shadow_block(..., &inc)` is followed by `if (inc) inc_children(info->tm, result->n, &le64_type);`, but that protection is not used in this collapse path. Thus the vulnerable construct is present: pointers are copied from child to parent without corresponding child-reference increments, and then the child block refcount is decremented. Therefore this version contains the bug and does not yet contain the fix.
